Counsel for Appellant :- Jitendra Singh Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Abhai Kumar Singh Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
List revised.
None appeared on behalf of the respondent even in the revised call except learned A.G.A. for the State.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 27.09.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Shahjahanpur.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case for committing rape with the victim.

Further submitted that the victim Sudhir Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92684037/
1 was major at the time of alleged incident and lodged the present F.I.R. herself after delay of 16 days without any explanation thereto.

entities.text: Sudhir Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The statement of the victim was recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. before the learned court concerned in which she stated that she was acquainted with the appellant prior to the alleged incident and as there was promise of marriage on the part of the appellant with the victim that was the reason there were transactions of money between both of them.
Later on, she made demand of money from the appellant which he refused and insulted her, thereafter, without her consent he committed rape with her alongwith one unknown person.

It is also submitted that statement of the victim shows that she was major, willing and consenting party but on account of dispute between both of them the present F.I.R. was lodged with false allegation of committing rape.
No any video was prepared by the appellant and no any such threat was given to her for making it viral.
Entire allegations levelled in the F.I.R. and in the statement are false.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
Appellant is in jail since 07.09.2023 having two cases as criminal history in which he is already on bail.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the order passed by learned Special Judge, the version in F.I.R., the delay in lodging the F.I.R. and the statement made by the victim u/s 164 Cr.P.C., the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order dated 27.09.2023 suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant- Sudhir Singh involved in Case Crime No.464 of 2023, under Sections 406, 452,
376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Shahjahanpur, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
